methods.description: has similar compute explosion, but clearly better accuracy

methods.name: AQ-NBEATS-OUT
methods.description: has comparable accuracy, but compute cost is multiplied by a factor of Q only for one of the blocks, making it order of magnitude more compute efficient

methods.name: parametric approach
methods.description: assumes a certain PDF for the forecast distribution and involves a forecasting model that produces 5 parameters of this PDF

methods.name: Gaussian processes
methods.description: a viable option for slightly more general modeling

methods.name: Student-t distribution
methods.description: can be used on top of MLP, DeepAR and Transformer models

methods.name: Gaussian mixture model
methods.description: another approach to handling multi-modality and asymmetry of forecast distribution

methods.name: Naive
methods.description: Uses the mean of the normal distribution of possible future values as the point forecast and estimates the standard deviation using the standard deviation of residuals.

methods.name: ARIMA
methods.description: Fitted using auto.arima() function in the forecast package, quantiles derived using forecast() function.

methods.name: ES
methods.description: Fitted using ets() function in the forecast package, quantiles derived using forecast() function.

methods.name: Theta method
methods.description: Estimates quantiles through bootstrapping using dotm() function in the forecTheta package.

methods.name: Neural models
methods.description: Sourced from GluonTS, a Python package for probabilistic time-series modeling.

methods.name: AQ-NBEATS-CAT
methods.description: Quantile level is appended as one of the elements in the input time-series history.

methods.name: AQ-ESRNN
methods.description: Model with global and time-series specific learnable parameters, uses learning rate scheduling and has a configurable number of layers.

methods.name: novel approach to probabilistic forecasting
methods.description: applicable to a variety of machine learning models, enabling a model to produce an arbitrary quantile at inference time
